headline: IEC proposes sanctions for election lies
script: Yo, if you're planning to vote in this year's local government elections, listen up. The IEC just dropped new proposals that could see political parties and candidates sanctioned for spreading deliberate election disinformation. Basically, parties caught lying to win your vote could face real consequences. Why does this matter to you? These elections are just months away, and disinformation targets young voters hardest, right there on your timeline. Meanwhile, accountability is in the spotlight too. Public Protector Kholeka Gcaleka is calling for people behind 'sextortion' schemes to be charged with corruption, not just lesser crimes. That's a bigger deterrent, and a sign the state is taking digital exploitation seriously. Stay informed, stay registered, and don't let anyone play you. That's politics, in 60.
why_it_matters: New IEC anti-disinformation rules directly affect what you can trust in your feed ahead of the local government elections.
